afirmacoes.texto: No primeiro ano de doutorado em Berkeley, Dantzig chegou atrasado à aula de Neyman, copiou dois problemas do quadro achando que eram dever de casa e entregou dias depois, pedindo desculpas pela demora.
afirmacoes.como: Li o PDF (Albers e Reid, 'An Interview with George B. Dantzig: The Father of Linear Programming', College Mathematics Journal 17(4), 1986, p. 300-301). Dantzig: 'during my first year at Berkeley I arrived late one day at one of Neyman's classes. On the blackboard there were two problems [that I] assumed had been assigned for homework. I copied them down. A few days later I apologized to Neyman for taking so long to do the homework'. Relato do próprio Dantzig. Não pus o ano (1939) na peça: a entrevista só diz 'At Berkeley in 1939' ao falar do departamento.

afirmacoes.texto: Eram dois problemas famosos da estatística, ainda sem solução (problemas em aberto).
afirmacoes.como: Entrevista: 'the problems on the blackboard that I had solved thinking they were homework were in fact two famous unsolved problems in statistics.' Dantzig repete em 'Linear Programming', Operations Research 50(1), 2002: 'My thesis was on two famous unsolved problems in mathematical statistics which I mistakenly thought were a homework assignment and solved.'

afirmacoes.texto: Seis semanas depois, num domingo às oito da manhã, Neyman bateu na porta para mandar um dos trabalhos para publicação; um ano depois, aceitou os dois como tese.
afirmacoes.como: Entrevista: 'About six weeks later, one Sunday morning about eight o'clock, Anne and I were awakened by someone banging on our front door. It was Neyman. [...] "I've just written an introduction to one of your papers. Read it so I can send it out right away for publication."' e 'A year later [...] Neyman just shrugged and told me to wrap the two problems in a binder and he would accept them as my thesis.'

afirmacoes.texto: Planejando para a Força Aérea dos EUA, Dantzig propôs o simplex em 1947.
afirmacoes.como: Li o PDF (G. B. Dantzig, 'Linear Programming', Operations Research 50(1), 2002, cópia do Wayback Machine): 'I proposed the simplex method in the summer 1947. But it took nearly a year before my colleagues and I in the Pentagon realized just how powerful the method really was.' e 'When I first analyzed the Air Force planning problem and saw that it could be formulated as a system of linear inequalities, I called my paper Programming in a Linear Structure.'

afirmacoes.texto: 'Programa' era jargão militar para planos de treino, suprimento e tropas; o termo veio antes do programa de computador, cujas instruções se chamavam 'códigos'.
afirmacoes.como: Mesmo texto, seção 'Origins of certain terms': 'The military refer to their various plans or proposed schedules of training, logistical supply and deployment of combat units as a program. [...] Note that the term program was used for linear programs long before it was used as the set of instructions used by a computer. In the early days, these instructions were called codes.'

afirmacoes.texto: Em 1948, Koopmans sugeriu o nome 'Linear Programming'.
afirmacoes.como: Mesmo texto: 'In the summer of 1948, Koopmans and I visited the Rand Corporation. One day we took a stroll along the Santa Monica beach. Koopmans said: "Why not shorten 'Programming in a Linear Structure' to 'Linear Programming'?"'

afirmacoes.texto: A aula do simplex no canal mostra como o algoritmo anda de vértice em vértice e como montar a tabela inicial.
afirmacoes.como: videos/simplex/metadados.json: 'ALGORITMO SIMPLEX - Como Funciona e a Tabela Inicial', gancho 'caminha de vértice em vértice até o ótimo [...] como montar a tabela Simplex inicial'; publicacao.json diz privacidade public.
